summary: Practise team structures, incident action plans, and multi-agency coordination. Explore the five-day disaster response training outline.
lede: Disaster response coordination aligns emergency managers, field leaders, and humanitarian coordinators around teams and information during incidents. Training covers team structures and incident action plans, resource requests through emergency operations centers, and situation reporting with QGIS mapping. Scenario exercises also practise needs assessment using KoboToolbox, partner responsibility mapping, and operational handovers, producing coordination matrices and operational briefings.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who organize or support disaster response operations and need reliable ways to align teams, information, and partner decisions. This course is designed for: Emergency Operations Center Coordinators managing incident objectives and inter-agency tasking. Disaster Response Team Leaders assigning field roles and tracking operational priorities. Humanitarian Coordination Officers linking agency plans through the OCHA Cluster Approach. Incident Planning Officers preparing action plans and operational briefings. Emergency Logistics Coordinators routing resource requests and tracking response constraints. Search and Rescue Team Coordinators aligning deployments with INSARAG Guidelines. Emergency Information Management Officers maintaining situation reports and shared incident data. Disaster Risk Management Officers connecting response activities with Sendai Framework priorities. Public Health Emergency Coordinators aligning health teams with response operations. Local Response Liaison Officers coordinating community requests with field team assignments.
prerequisites: Prior experience in emergency management, humanitarian response, public safety, health emergency operations, or a related coordination role is recommended. No coding is required. Bring familiarity with incident reporting or team coordination; digital mapping and data collection exercises use QGIS and KoboToolbox as proposed practice environments, with access arrangements confirmed before delivery.
